items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: One of my favorite ladies that I saw at the Graystone Ballroom was Miss Lil Green.

ctx.x: No, that was Lil Green. Lil Green did her... In fact, her first two hits she covered Lil Green. Yeah, Lil Green; that's Lil Green's thing. She was something. She talked plenty of street talk! [LAUGHS] I think she was a little ahead of her time. She was talking over a lot of people's heads!

Let's see. I started working with a bass player out of Columbus, Ohio, named Tweed(?) Beard around this time. And he was... He wasn't the greatest bass player, but he could make a great presentation, you know, and he was a pretty boy and everything. And he always had good guys around him. That's just about the time when Glenn Miller was really getting hot, you know, with "String of Pearls" and all those things.
